title: Add JSON Schema response_format, strict mode validation, and improved error messages
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add 'response_format' support with JSON Schema validation and a 'strict' mode. API returns clear validation error codes when generation doesn't conform; OpenAI-compat layer maps to response_format/strict. Backwards-compatible unless strict=true. See docs for migration notes.
description:
Summary: Adds first-class support for JSON Schema-based structured output via a new response_format API parameter, introduces a strict validation mode, improves error messages and status codes for schema violations, and updates the OpenAI compatibility layer to map function-calling/response_format behavior. Motivation: users require deterministic, machine-parseable outputs for downstream parsing and tooling. This PR implements server-side validation and clear developer-facing errors to reduce post-processing complexity.

What changed (high level): - API surface: new response_format parameter (supports 'json_schema' object with fields: schema, strict:boolean, on_failure:string) and response.schema_validation_status in response metadata. - Validation: model-generated outputs are validated against the provided JSON Schema. Modes: permissive (default) - returns best-effort output and validation metadata; strict - enforces validity and returns a 422 with structured error payload when generation fails to produce valid JSON. - Streaming: when streaming is used with strict=true, the server buffers chunks and only streams validated JSON; if validation fails we abort stream with a structured final message. For permissive streaming we stream tokens as before and annotate validation metadata at end-of-stream. - OpenAI-compat: added translation layer for 'response_format' parameter and existing function-calling semantics so clients using the OpenAI-compatible API get equivalent behavior. - Errors: introduces schema_validation_failed and schema_parse_error error codes, with detailed path and message lists for debugging. - Docs/tests: Extended API docs, added end-to-end tests and schema fuzz tests.

Checklist: - [x] API contract defined and documented - [x] Server-side validation implementation - [x] Streaming behavior covered and tested - [x] OpenAI compatibility mapping implemented - [x] Unit and integration tests added - [x] Docs updated (api/structured-output.md)

Design notes: - We validate using AJV on the server before returning final responses. For strict mode we only return success when validation passes; otherwise we return HTTP 422 with a JSON error body that includes schema_validation_errors (array of {path, message, keyword}). For permissive mode we always return generated text and include validation metadata under response.schema_validation_status (valid|invalid) and schema_validation_errors. - Streaming: strict streaming required buffering to avoid sending invalid partial results. We buffer up to a configurable byte limit (default 64KB) and then attempt validation; if it does not validate we continue to attempt reconstitution until an end-of-stream or buffer limit breach. When buffer limit is exceeded without successful validation we abort with schema_validation_failed. - OpenAI compatibility: when incoming OpenAI-style function schemas are provided we convert them into our response_format JSON Schema shape and set strict=true when caller requested exact function output.

Backward compatibility and migration: - Default behavior remains permissive to avoid breaking existing customers. - Customers opting into strict mode should expect 422 responses on invalid output and should handle schema_validation_errors accordingly. - Release notes contain examples for migrating function-calling flows to response_format.

Related work: Linear ENG-4512 (schema validation), ENG-4590 (streaming stability for structured output).

Additional implementation details and examples are in the changed files list and api docs updated in this PR.

2) feat(runtime): integrate AJV-based validator with generation pipeline
3) feat(streaming): buffer-and-validate logic for strict streaming mode
4) feat(openai-compat): map OpenAI function schemas to response_format
5) test: add e2e structured output tests and schema fuzz tests
6) docs: api/structured-output.md and migration guide
7) fix(tests): address flaky streaming test after buffering tweak

runtime/streaming/stream_buffer.py: buffer until chunk_end or max_bytes, attempt validation, abort stream with structured error if strict and invalid

Ben Thompson: 'Tests are thorough. One nit: please add an explicit test for nested arrays and large schema refs.'
Aisha Patel: 'Added test for nested arrays and a test with $ref using local schema bundle.'

notes_for_release: Server: response_format JSON Schema support with optional strict mode. Default permissive validation preserves backwards compatibility. Clients using strict mode should handle 422 schema_validation_failed errors. OpenAI-compat maps function schemas to response_format; consult migration guide in docs.
